OpenShellPolicy spec.networkPolicies=[{"name":"web","endpoints":[]}]

OpenShellPolicy spec.networkPolicies=[{"name":"web","endpoints":[{"host":"example.com","port":0}]}]
  OpenShellPolicy p: every endpoint needs a host, a port from 1 to 65535, protocol rest or none, and access read-only, read-write or none
OpenShellPolicy spec.networkPolicies=[{"name":"web","endpoints":[{"host":"example.com","port":443}],"binaries":[]}]
  OpenShellPolicy p: binaries, when set, are 1 to 16 paths
Grant spec.secrets=[{"name":"k","key":"k","deliver":"inject","to":{"host":"*.example.com"}}]
  Grant g: secret k: to.host "*.example.com" must be one host name
Grant spec.secrets=[{"name":"k","key":"k","deliver":"inject","to":{"host":"a.example.com","format":"Bearer"}}]
  Grant g: secret k: to.format must contain {{value}} once
Grant spec.secrets=[{"name":"k","key":"k","deliver":"inject","to":{"host":"a.example.com","header":"X: y"}}]
  Grant g: secret k: to.header "X: y" isn't a header name
Grant spec.secrets=[{"name":"k","key":"k","deliver":"file","path":"/run/s,src=/,dst=/run/q/f"}]
  Grant g: secret k: path "/run/s,src=/,dst=/run/q/f" must be under /run/ (tmpfs: a secret file never reaches the silo's disk), a clean path of letters, digits, . _ - and /
Grant spec.secrets=[{"name":"k","key":"k","deliver":"file","path":"/run/s/a:b"}]
  Grant g: secret k: path "/run/s/a:b" must be under /run/ (tmpfs: a secret file never reaches the silo's disk), a clean path of letters, digits, . _ - and /
Grant spec.secrets=[{"name":"k","key":"k","deliver":"file","path":"/etc/k"}]
  Grant g: secret k: path "/etc/k" must be under /run/ (tmpfs: a secret file never reaches the silo's disk), a clean path of letters, digits, . _ - and /
IngressClass spec.controller.driver=""
  IngressClass public: spec.controller.driver names the proxy's driver (nginx, caddy, kong…)
IngressClass spec.controller.siloSet="ingress"
  IngressClass public: spec.controller needs its namespace and one of silo or siloSet
Ingress spec.ingressClass=""
  Ingress i: spec.ingressClass is required
Ingress spec.hosts=[]
  Ingress i: spec.hosts needs at least one host name
Ingress spec.rules=[{"service":{"name":"web","port":""}}]
  Ingress i: every rule needs a service (its name) and one of its ports (by name)
Ingress spec.rules.0.path="api"
  Ingress i: paths start with /
Ingress spec.tls={"issuer":"a","secretName":"b"}
  Ingress i: tls: at most one of issuer, secretName or none (none of them: the cluster's default issuer for the class)
Ingress spec.hosts=["10.0.0.1"]
  Ingress i: spec.hosts: "10.0.0.1" isn't a host name
Issuer spec.controller="acme"
  Issuer ca: an Issuer names one cert-controller: controller (with config), or the shorthand acme or internalCA
Issuer spec.internalCA! spec.acme={"server":"http://acme.example.com/dir"}
  Issuer ca: acme.server is an https:// directory URL
Issuer spec.internalCA! spec.acme={"server":"https://acme.example.com/dir","solvers":[{}]}
  Issuer ca: each acme solver is exactly one of http01 or dns01
Issuer spec.internalCA! spec.acme={"server":"https://acme.example.com/dir","solvers":[{"dns01":{"provider":""}}]}
  Issuer ca: a dns01 solver names a DNS provider registered on the control plane
Certificate spec.hosts=[]
  Certificate c: spec.hosts needs at least one host name
Certificate spec.issuer=""
  Certificate c: spec.issuer and spec.secretName are required
Certificate spec.hosts=["a b"]
  Certificate c: spec.hosts: "a b" isn't a host name
Role rules=[{"verbs":[],"resources":["silos"]}]
  Role r: every rule needs verbs and resources
ClusterRole rules=[{"verbs":["sudo"],"resources":["silos"]}]
  ClusterRole r: verbs must be *, get, list, watch, create, update, patch, delete, or for secrets use, read-value, write and approve, for ips use, or for silos/exposure open and approve
Role rules=[{"verbs":["get"],"resources":["silos"],"selector":{"a":"b"}}]
  Role r: a rule's selector (by label) only works on secrets and silos/exposure
Role rules=[{"verbs":["get"],"resources":["clustersecrets"]}]
  Role r: a Role can't grant clustersecrets or clustersecrets/value: use a ClusterRole
Role rules=[{"verbs":["get"],"resources":["clustersecrets/value"]}]
  Role r: a Role can't grant clustersecrets or clustersecrets/value: use a ClusterRole
ClusterRole rules=[{"verbs":["get"]}]
  ClusterRole r: every rule needs verbs and resources (no such overload: size)
Role rules=[{"verbs":["sudo"],"resources":["silos"]}]
  Role r: verbs must be *, get, list, watch, create, update, patch, delete, or for secrets use, read-value, write and approve, for ips use, or for silos/exposure open and approve
ClusterRole rules=[{"verbs":["get"],"resources":["silos/exec"],"selector":{"a":"b"}}]
  ClusterRole r: a rule's selector (by label) only works on secrets and silos/exposure
ClusterRoleBinding roleRef.name=""
  ClusterRoleBinding b: roleRef.name is required
RoleBinding subjects=[]
  RoleBinding b: a binding needs at least one subject
ClusterRoleBinding subjects=[{"kind":"User","name":""}]
  ClusterRoleBinding b: every subject needs a name and a kind of User, Group or ServiceAccount
Service spec.type="ClusterIP"
  Service svc: type "ClusterIP": Internal (the default: a virtual IP on the mesh) or LoadBalancer (a provider's balancer in front)
Service spec.type="HostPort"
  Service svc: type HostPort arrives at the worker running one silo, so a Service of several can't be one: put a HostPort service in each silo's services (or the SiloSet's template, with own: true for an address each), or use type LoadBalancer for the group
Service spec.type="LoadBalancer"
  Service svc: type LoadBalancer needs loadBalancer.provider: the installed provider making the balancer (e.g. linode)
Service spec.loadBalancer={"provider":"linode"}
  Service svc: loadBalancer goes with type: LoadBalancer
Service spec.type="LoadBalancer" spec.loadBalancer={"provider":"Linode"}
  Service svc: loadBalancer.provider "Linode": an installed provider's name (e.g. linode)
RoleBinding roleRef.kind="Group"
  RoleBinding b: roleRef.kind must be Role or ClusterRole
ClusterRoleBinding roleRef.kind="Role"
  ClusterRoleBinding b: a ClusterRoleBinding can only grant a ClusterRole
RoleBinding roleRef.name=""
  RoleBinding b: roleRef.name is required
ClusterRoleBinding subjects=[]
  ClusterRoleBinding b: a binding needs at least one subject
RoleBinding subjects=[{"kind":"Robot","name":"r"}]
  RoleBinding b: every subject needs a name and a kind of User, Group or ServiceAccount
IP spec.type!
  IP ip: spec.type is required: Host (one of a host's extra addresses: hostAddress) or Provider (reserved from a provider: provider, region)
IP spec.type="Pool"
  IP ip: spec.type "Pool": Host or Provider
IP spec.hostAddress!
  IP ip: type Host needs hostAddress: the name of one of a host's extra addresses (kvoadm host addresses HOST add NAME ADDRESS)
IP spec.hostAddress="Mail"
  IP ip: spec.hostAddress "Mail": a host address's name (lower-case letters, digits, -)
IP spec.region="us-ord"
  IP ip: type Host is a host's address: provider and region are for type Provider (drop them, or make it type: Provider)
IP spec.type="Provider" spec.hostAddress! spec.provider="linode"
  IP ip: type Provider needs provider and region: the installed provider (e.g. linode) and where to reserve it (e.g. us-ord); never guessed
IP spec.type="Provider" spec.provider="linode" spec.region="us-ord"
  IP ip: type Provider is reserved from the provider: hostAddress is for type Host (drop it, or make it type: Host)
IP spec.type="Provider" spec.hostAddress! spec.provider="Linode" spec.region="us-ord"
  IP ip: spec.provider "Linode": an installed provider's name (e.g. linode)
IPSet spec.type!
  IPSet ips: spec.type is required: Static (members you list) or Dynamic (provider IPs reserved as instances need them)
IPSet spec.type="Pool"
  IPSet ips: spec.type "Pool": Static or Dynamic
IPSet spec.members=[]
  IPSet ips: type Static needs members: one per instance, each { ip: NAME } or { hostAddress: NAME }
IPSet spec.members=[{"ip":"a","hostAddress":"b"}]
  IPSet ips: members[0]: exactly one of ip (an IP's name) and hostAddress (a host address's name)
IPSet spec.members=[{"ip":"a"},{"ip":"a"}]
  IPSet ips: members[1]: ip: a is members[0] already: one address per ordinal
IPSet spec.max=3
  IPSet ips: type Static lists its members: provider, region and max are for type Dynamic
IPSet spec.type="Dynamic" spec.provider="linode" spec.region="us-ord" spec.max=2
  IPSet ips: type Dynamic reserves provider IPs, so it can't have a host's address (hostAddress b): use type Static with hostAddress members; type Dynamic has no members: Kevaso reserves them as instances need them (SET-0, SET-1, …); list them with type Static instead
IPSet spec.type="Dynamic" spec.members! spec.provider="linode"
  IPSet ips: type Dynamic needs provider, region and max (at least 1): who reserves the IPs, where, and how many at most
Host spec.internalIP!
  Host h: a host needs spec.internalIP (its address on its own network), spec.externalIP (its address reachable from outside it), or both
Host spec.components={}
  Host h: a host needs at least one component: controlPlane or worker
Host spec.components.worker={"taints":[{"key":"k","effect":"NoExecute"}]}
  Host h: every taint needs a key and an effect of NoSchedule or PreferNoSchedule (there's no NoExecute: silos are stateful)
Host spec.components.worker={"runtimes":[{"name":"kvm"}]}
  Host h: unknown runtime in spec.components.worker.runtimes
Host spec.internalIP="fd00::1"
  Host h: spec.internalIP: "fd00::1" isn't an IPv4 address
Host spec.externalIP="10.0.0.5"
  Host h: spec.internalIP and spec.externalIP are the same address: a machine with one address has one of the two (external if it's reachable from outside its network)
Host spec.network={"dns":["mesh"]}
  Host h: spec.network.dns: "mesh": internal or external (silos and the mesh are always answered)
Host spec.network={"dns":["external"]}
  Host h: spec.network.dns: external: the host has no external IP
Host spec.addresses=[{"name":"mail","kind":"external","address":"nope"}]
  Host h: spec.addresses[0]: "nope" isn't an address
Host spec.addresses=[{"name":"mail","kind":"external","address":"203.0.113.0/30"}]
  Host h: spec.addresses[0]: "203.0.113.0/30" is a range: one address per name (add each with its own name)
Host spec.addresses=[{"name":"mail","kind":"public","address":"203.0.113.9"}]
  Host h: spec.addresses[0]: kind "public": external (reachable from outside the host's network) or internal
Host spec.addresses=[{"name":"Mail","kind":"external","address":"203.0.113.9"}]
  Host h: spec.addresses[0]: name "Mail": lower-case letters, digits and - (an IP of type Host names it)
Host spec.addresses=[{"name":"a","kind":"external","address":"203.0.113.9"},{"name":"a","kind":"external","address":"203.0.113.10"}]
  Host h: spec.addresses[1]: a is listed twice
Host spec.addresses=[{"name":"a","kind":"internal","address":"10.0.0.5"}]
  Host h: spec.addresses[0]: 10.0.0.5 is its main IP already
Namespace metadata.name="mesh"
  Namespace mesh: "mesh" is a network's name (mesh, internal, external), which names use as a label of their own: pick another
Namespace metadata.name="internal"
  Namespace internal: "internal" is a network's name (mesh, internal, external), which names use as a label of their own: pick another
Namespace metadata.name="external"
  Namespace external: "external" is a network's name (mesh, internal, external), which names use as a label of their own: pick another
